newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in brisk trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in brisk trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Tuesday on hopes for continued declining inflation and falling interest rates, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.11 pct to 102.68
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 101.66.
Volume was a high 192 million shekels with activity in the Makams alone reaching 85 million shekels.
"The market continues to rise because investors believe that the Bank of Israel will have to lower its key lending rate," said Ari Eidelheit of Zeller Eblagon Securities.
"There are almost no sellers on the market," said Gila Shkury of Israel Discount Bank.

She said CPI-linked bonds rose across the board on hopes that the central bank would reduce interest rates. "Inflation is expected to remain relatively low over the next three months and the rate is expected to decline," Shkury added.
Traders noted that yields on medium and long CPI bonds fell to 4.1-4.2 percent, which is relatively low.
Unlinked bonds and Makams also rose. "This is realy crazy. I do not understand why investors are so eager to buy Makams, which offer a yield of only 13.63 percent," said one trader.
Shkury said dollar-linked bonds continued to rise, with almost all the activity concentrated in short bonds, as investors expect that the dollar will continue to rise against the shekel.
On Tuesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3160 shekels against 3.3210 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
